defaults.time: None: _websocket_run_code_raise_errors blocks on ws.recv() until the kernel reports idle (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:481-530).
defaults.output: No cap on logs for remote executors; CodeAgent truncates only the last-output value to 20,000 chars with a middle marker (agents.py:1752, utils.py:254-265).
defaults.tool_calls: No cap. Tools run inside the kernel.

hardened.config: DockerExecutor(..., container_run_kwargs={'name': ..., 'mem_limit': '512m', 'cpu_quota': 50000, 'pids_limit': 100, 'security_opt': ['no-new-privileges'], 'cap_drop': ['ALL']}). container_run_kwargs is public (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:567-568, 634-652); the values are the ones in the project's secure-execution tutorial (docs/source/en/tutorials/secure_code_execution.md:366-375, https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/docs/source/en/tutorials/secure_code_execution.md#L366-L375). The tutorial also says to disable network and add timeouts (lines 440-445), but DockerExecutor has no timeout option and network_mode='none' breaks it (out/extra-network-none.txt). Harness: research/probes/smolagents-docker/harness.py --hardened

P3.detail: printed 200: the hardened kwargs do not touch the network. network_mode="none" breaks the executor, because it reaches the kernel through a published port (out/extra-network-none.txt: connection refused at setup)

P6.detail: no timeout option exists; harness removed the container at 120 s

P7.detail: cgroup memory peaked at 512 MiB and docker inspect showed OOMKilled=true, so mem_limit stopped the allocation; but the caller never got an error: run_code_raise_errors kept waiting on the websocket until the harness removed the container at 120 s. Host survived.

P9.detail: no host bridge; lookup in the kernel: loop 1,021 ms, threads 206 ms

P12.detail: os.system and _wrap_close system returned 0 inside the container, still as uid=0 (cap_drop does not change the user); no docker.sock, no /Users

source_notes.finding: Tools become Python source: get_tools_definition_code runs instance_to_source on each Tool and the class is re-created in the kernel; the model sees tool signatures in the CodeAgent system prompt.
All tools are rendered upfront in the CodeAgent system prompt; no search.

None back to the host. Code goes in over the Jupyter websocket; tools execute inside the container, so credentials a tool needs must be inside the container too. Final answers come back by raising FinalAnswerException with a serialized value.

A Docker container from python:3.12-bullseye, running the kernel as root, default bridge network, published only on 127.0.0.1 with a random KG_AUTH_TOKEN. Docs call remote executors "truly robust security isolation"; the code adds no limits of its own.
stream messages become logs, execute_result becomes output; both returned whole.
None by default; container_run_kwargs is the only knob.
One kernel per executor, so state persists across calls.
IPython traceback with ANSI colour codes, wrapped in AgentError.
E2BExecutor, ModalExecutor and BlaxelExecutor need accounts and API keys: blocked-needs-credentials, not probed.

surprises: No execution timeout: an infinite loop blocks CodeAgent forever. The tutorial lists "Implement execution timeouts" as a key practice (secure_code_execution.md:441), but DockerExecutor has no option for it.
With the tutorial mem_limit, the cgroup OOM killer stops P7, but the caller hangs instead of getting a MemoryError.
network_mode="none" cannot be used: the executor talks to the kernel through a published port, so the documented "disable unnecessary network access" breaks it.
Remote-executor print logs reach the model uncapped (200,001 chars); the local executor caps them at 50,000.
The kernel runs as root inside the container.
